text: Medic four on scene, roughly 30 year old male found unresponsive in a public restroom, bystanders suspect an overdose.
He's not responding to voice or sternal rub, respirations are slow and shallow, about six a minute, pinpoint pupils.
SpO2 is 82 percent, heart rate 58, blood pressure 104 over 62, we're bagging him now.
No allergy information available, no bystanders know his history.
No real change after two minutes, still minimal respiratory effort.
Administering a second dose of naloxone, another 0.4 milligrams intranasal.
Now he's starting to breathe on his own, SpO2 coming up to 93 percent, acuity level one.
ETA to the ED about twelve minutes, oh two forty, will update on arrival.
